1.name: Spellcasting
1.notes:
You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation.

Cantrips. You know three cantrips of your choice from the Cleric spell list. Guidance, Sacred Flame, and Thaumaturgy are recommended. Whenever you gain a Cleric level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another Cleric cantrip of your choice. At Cleric levels 4 and 10, you learn one additional cantrip, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Cleric Features table.

Spell Slots. The Cleric Features table shows how many spell slots you have for your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare a list of Cleric spells of level 1+ that you can cast. To start, choose four level 1 Cleric spells. Bless, Cure Wounds, Guiding Bolt, and Shield of Faith are recommended. The number of prepared spells increases with your Cleric level, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Cleric Features table. Prepared spells must be of levels for which you have spell slots. If a Cleric feature gives you spells that are always prepared, they don’t count against this number but are still Cleric spells for you.

Changing Prepared Spells. When you finish a Long Rest, you can change your prepared list, replacing any number of prepared spells with other Cleric spells for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Cleric spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use a Holy Symbol as a Spellcasting Focus for your Cleric spells.

1.name: Divine Order
1.notes:
You dedicate yourself to one sacred role: Protector or Thaumaturge, gaining benefits based on your choice.

Protector. You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Heavy armor.

Thaumaturge. You know one extra Cleric cantrip. In addition, you add your Wisdom modifier (minimum +1) as a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) checks.

2.name: Channel Divinity
2.notes:
You can use Channel Divinity to fuel magical effects, such as Divine Spark and Turn Undead. You can use this class’s Channel Divinity twice, regaining one use on a Short Rest and all uses on a Long Rest. At higher levels, you gain additional uses as shown in the Channel Divinity column of the Cleric Features table. Channel Divinity save DCs use your Cleric spell save DC.

Divine Spark. As a Magic action, you target a creature within 30 feet and roll 1d8 + your Wisdom modifier. You either heal that amount or force the target to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice) equal to the total; on a success, it takes half as much damage, rounded down. The damage increases to 2d8 + your Wisdom modifier at level 7, 3d8 + your Wisdom modifier at level 13, and 4d8 + your Wisdom modifier at level 18.

Turn Undead. As a Magic action, you present your Holy Symbol and choose any number of Undead within 30 feet of yourself. Each chosen Undead must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is Frightened and Incapacitated for up to 1 minute and must use its movement to move away from you on its turns. The effect ends early if the creature takes any damage, if you become Incapacitated, or if you die.

3.name: Life Domain Spells
3.notes: You always have the listed spells prepared when you reach the specified Cleric level. See spell_table for details.

3.name: Disciple of Life
3.notes: When you cast a spell with a spell slot that restores Hit Points, the target regains additional Hit Points equal to 2 + the spell slot's level on the turn you cast the spell.

3.name: Preserve Life
3.notes: As a Magic action, you present your Holy Symbol and expend Channel Divinity to restore Hit Points equal to 5 × your Cleric level. Choose Bloodied creatures within 30 feet and divide the healing among them. This feature can’t raise a creature above half its Hit Point maximum.

5.name: Sear Undead
5.notes: Whenever you use Turn Undead, roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1d8). Each Undead that fails its saving throw against that use of Turn Undead takes Radiant damage equal to the total rolled. This damage does not end the Turn Undead effect.

6.name: Blessed Healer
6.notes: When you cast a healing spell on another creature using a spell slot, you regain Hit Points equal to 2 + the spell slot's level.

7.name: Blessed Strikes
7.notes:
You gain one of the following options: Divine Strike or Potent Spellcasting.

Divine Strike. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice).

Potent Spellcasting. You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Cleric cantrip.

10.name: Divine Intervention
10.notes: As a Magic action, you choose a Cleric spell of level 5 or lower that does not require a Reaction and cast it without expending a spell slot or needing Material components. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

traits.name: Dwarven Resilience
traits.notes: You have Resistance to Poison damage. You also have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.

traits.name: Dwarven Toughness
traits.notes: Your Hit Point maximum increases by 1, and it increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level.

traits.name: Stonecunning
traits.notes: As a Bonus Action, you gain Tremorsense with a range of 60 feet for 10 minutes. You must be on a stone surface or touching a stone surface to use this Tremorsense. The stone can be natural or worked. You can use this Bonus Action a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

feats.notes: Tool Proficiency. You gain proficiency with three different Artisan's Tools of your choice from the Fast Crafting table.Discount. Whenever you buy a nonmagical item, you receive a 20 percent discount on it.Fast Crafting. When you finish a Long Rest, you can craft one piece of gear from the Fast Crafting table, provided you have the Artisan's Tools associated with that item and have proficiency with those tools. The item lasts until you finish another Long Rest, at which point the item falls apart.
feats.name: Crafter

feats.notes: Armor Training. You gain training with Light armor and Shields.
feats.name: Lightly Armored

feats.notes: ore Knowledge. Choose one of the following skills: Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, or Religion. If you lack proficiency in the chosen skill, you gain proficiency in it, and if you already have proficiency in it, you gain Expertise in it.Quick Study. You can take the Study action as a Bonus Action.
feats.name: Keen Mind
